cards.text: Paul, an apostle, is writing to the church of God in Corinth (1 Corinthians 1:1-2). He's just shown them that Christ has indeed been raised from the dead (1 Corinthians 15:20). Now he sees the next question coming: "How are the dead raised? With what kind of body will they come?"
Paul skips the warm-up and starts his answer with two words: "You fool!" Then he heads straight out to the field: "What you sow does not come to life unless it dies."

cards.question: Paul says the seed you sow is just a seed, not the body it will become.
A little seed of wheat goes in the ground. Who does Paul say gives it the body it comes up with?
Next Paul looks at men, animals, birds and fish. What does he say about their flesh?

answers.text: Men and animals share one kind

cards.text: Paul keeps going. There are heavenly bodies and earthly bodies, he says, and their splendor is not of the same degree.

cards.question: Up in the sky, Paul says the sun, the moon and every single star all share the same splendor.

cards.text: Seed, flesh, sun, moon, STARS, and then Paul lands it: "So will it be with the resurrection of the dead…"

cards.question: Paul says the body that is sown is perishable, and it is raised ___.
Paul keeps going about the body that is sown and raised. He says it is sown in dishonor and raised in ___.

cards.text: Then Paul adds that the body is sown in weakness and raised in power. Baker, I sat for years in a junk drawer with my edges worn soft, so that line has my mustache doing a LITTLE DANCE.

cards.question: Paul says what is sown is a natural body. What kind of body does he say is raised?

cards.text: Then Paul goes all the way back to the very first man. He quotes Genesis 2:7: "The first man Adam became a living being".

cards.question: After the first man Adam, Paul says there is also a last Adam. What does Paul call the last Adam?
Paul says the natural came first, and then the spiritual.

cards.text: Now Paul sets two men side by side. The first man was of the dust of the earth.

cards.question: The first man was of the dust of the earth. Where does Paul say the second man is from?

cards.text: As was the earthly man, so are those of the earth, and as is the heavenly man, so are those of heaven. Paul says we've borne the likeness of the earthly man, and we shall bear the likeness of the heavenly man too.

cards.question: Paul tells the brothers that flesh and blood can inherit the kingdom of God just as it is.

cards.text: Then Paul leans in close: "Listen, I tell you a mystery…" Not all of us will sleep, he says.

cards.question: Paul's mystery: we will not all sleep, but we will all be ___.
Paul says we will all be changed. How fast does he say it happens?

answers.text: In the twinkling of an eye
At the turning of a year
In the passing of a day

cards.text: It will happen at the last trumpet, when the dead will be raised imperishable and we will be changed. The twinkling of an eye, baker, and it takes me longer than that to FIND MY APRON!

cards.question: Paul says the perishable must be clothed with the imperishable, and the mortal with ___.

cards.text: Paul says that once the perishable has been clothed with the imperishable, a saying that is written will come to pass. Paul quotes Isaiah 25:8.

cards.question: When the perishable is clothed with the imperishable, Paul says a written saying will come to pass. What does that saying say happens to death?

answers.text: It is swallowed up in victory
It is held back for a season
It is cast out of the land

cards.text: Then Paul quotes Hosea 13:14, words that talk straight to death. To DEATH, baker: "Where, O Death, is your victory? Where, O Death, is your sting?"

cards.question: Death's sting just came up. Paul says the sting of death is ___.

cards.text: Paul adds that the power of sin is the law, then goes from the sting straight to the shout: "But thanks be to God, who gives us the victory through our Lord Jesus Christ!" Baker, I didn't CLIMB out of the junk drawer I was forgotten in, I got CALLED out of it!
So now what? Paul tells his beloved brothers to be steadfast and immovable and always excel in the work of the Lord, which in my bakery means KEEP THOSE OVENS HOT.

cards.question: Paul tells the brothers to always excel in the work of the Lord. Why?

answers.text: Their labor in the Lord is not in vain
Others will see their good work
Their reward will come in this life
